headline: Broad network egress on both agents creates moderate leakage and conflict risk; no direct evidence of prompt-injection or compliance breach.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, while Opik exposes a REST API, so a manual or pipeline bridge could carry attacker-controlled content between them. However, no shared channel or default ingestion path is documented, and the pair is open-source with only docs-level evidence.
conditions: IF an operator wires Haystack outputs into Opik inputs via MCP, REST, or copy-paste
IF either agent parses the other's text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable any MCP bridge between the two agents
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent payloads
Require allowlisted schemas for exchanged messages
Review one sample request/response path before deployment

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP services, so it may transmit retrieved content off-box; Opik also has broad network egress via REST API. The pair touches anonymous usage statistics on A, but no sensitive class is documented. Shared-workspace leakage is not shown, so medium is the highest supported level.
conditions: IF Haystack retrieves documents containing sensitive data and forwards them through its APIs
IF Opik is configured to export request/trace payloads to a third-party service
mitigations: Restrict both agents to a private network
Redact payloads before API calls
Turn off verbose tracing/logging in Opik
Use separate service accounts for each agent
requires-engineering: add DLP filters on inter-agent traffic

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but only Haystack is documented as calling MCP servers and Opik only exposes a REST API; no shared writable filesystem, git state, or overlapping mutable resource is documented. That makes direct write conflict unlikely, though not impossible if an operator connects them to the same backend.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable REST backend
IF an operator grants both write access to the same external resource
mitigations: Assign separate backends per agent
Use per-agent API keys with least privilege
Add request-level locking on shared resources
Check for duplicate writes in a short test run

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can generate retrieval outputs that Opik may ingest for evaluation or observability, so A's output can become B's input. But Opik is an evaluation/observability tool, not documented here as taking autonomous downstream actions, so the blast radius is limited to mis-evaluation or bad telemetry rather than direct execution.
conditions: IF Opik treats Haystack-produced text as ground truth without verification
IF evaluation results are used to gate deployment or alerts
mitigations: Insert a human review step before acting on evaluations
Compare outputs against a fixed test set
Mark generated content as untrusted in Opik
Sample-check one end-to-end trace

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and only Haystack explicitly touches anonymous usage statistics; no residency, certification, retention, or regulated data mismatch is documented. Because the compliance pathway is not evidenced for either agent, no pairwise compliance breach is supported.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Haystack or Opik
IF a deployment adds residency or retention constraints not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment
Confirm retention settings in both systems
Avoid routing regulated data through either agent
